title: The bishop

card.idea: The bishop slides along diagonals, as far as the road is clear. Because a diagonal never changes colour, a bishop keeps the colour it starts on for the whole game. Each side has one for the light squares and one for the dark.

explain.text: Diagonals only. From d4 the bishop runs up-right to h8, up-left to a7, down-left to a1 and down-right to g1. Every square it touches is a dark square.
Your own pawn on b2 blocks one road, so c3 is as far as the bishop goes that way. The black pawn on f2 does not block: the bishop takes it and stops there.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square the bishop can move to.
challenges.reason: Four diagonals out of d4, and every square on them is dark.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square the bishop can move to.
challenges.reason: Your own pawn stops you at c3; the black pawn on f2 is a square you can land on.

challenges.prompt: Tap the square where the bishop can take a pawn.
challenges.reason: Down the right-hand diagonal: e3, then the pawn on f2.

challenges.prompt: This bishop stands on a dark square. Which squares can it never reach, no matter how many moves it gets?
challenges.reason: A diagonal stays on one colour, so the other colour is off limits forever.

hints.text: Not the edge: from d4 the bishop can reach a1, a7, g1 and h8, and every one of those is on the rim.

wrong.Bd4: Same diagonal, but you stopped halfway and the rook walks away.
wrong.g3: A quiet pawn move while a rook is going free.

challenges.reason: The long diagonal from b2 runs straight into the rook.

wrong.Bc4: Nearly there. One more square along the diagonal and the knight is yours.
wrong.Kf1: Nothing wrong with the king, but the knight is free.

challenges.reason: b3, c4, d5: the knight is sitting on your diagonal.

takeaway: A bishop slides on diagonals and stays on its own colour all game.
